newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kohl sees no significant change in unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees no significant change in unemployment.

text.p: German chancellor Helmut Kohl said during a visit to New Zealand on Wednesday that he saw no significant change this year in the German unemployment trend.
"This year will not bring a change in the trend for the labour market, especially not as high as I would wish," Kohl told a news conference after talks with New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger.
Kohl repeated that his political goal was to halve unemployment by the year 2000. "It is our goal. I cannot say whether it will be reached."
His comments came after figures released on Tuesday showed a slight, seasonally-adjusted increase in German unemployment to 4.299 million in April.

Kohl's two-day visit to New Zealand, the first by a German chancellor, is part of his mission to strengthen links with Asia-Pacific countries. Kohl is accompanied by a 13-member delegation of leading business representatives who will be looking for trade opportunities during meetings with government ministers and New Zealand business representatives.

Bolger said the talks, covering bilateral issues, Europe and Asian Pacific affairs, were warm and wide-ranging. He said he saw Germany as the anchor of economic growth and trade liberalisation in the European Union.
